<description>
Alternative approach to #36688, citing the relevant parts of its description:

[quoted text omitted]
Fix this by ignoring the exceptionSet. Except on Windows, where we instead disconnect if its used.

We could instead have set `SO_OOBINLINE` on our sockets, so `recv()` returns any urgent data sent to us (and likely leads us to disconnect the peer). RFC 6093 doesn't forbid this, but the current approach seems more clear and direct to me.

The PR makes two additional changes for clarity:
- wrap the `FD_ISSET` check in `#ifdef WIN32` (no behavior change)
- instead of `if (recvSet || errorSet)`, check `errorSet` separately and earlier (emits a different log message)

Test coverage is introduced in `p2p_socket_errors.py`.

Finally a similar fix is applied to HTTP.
</description>

<commits>
7cc5f0a901 sock: guard select exception result handling with WIN32

The select() backend only adds sockets to the exception set on Windows.
Elsewhere, the set starts empty and remains empty after select(), so
checking it with FD_ISSET() is a no-op. Match the existing WIN32 guard
around FD_SET().

This commit does not change behavior.

9dce056e4a test: move send-stall wait into the framework

8d2825f7b0 test: cover P2P reset while sending

Reset a slow reader with block output stalled and more input queued
behind receive backpressure.

628a74e299 net: disconnect on poll errors before sending

Disconnect directly on POLLERR/POLLHUP without read readiness,
skipping the send attempt that would otherwise fail and disconnect
the peer. This also changes the debug log message.

Only call recv() for readable sockets.

2ec146efa0 test: cover P2P TCP urgent data handling

Check that urgent indications do not prevent ordinary P2P input from
being processed or count as received message bytes.

Co-authored-by: Matthew Zipkin <pinheadmz@pm.me>

a626b28980 net: stop monitoring select exceptions outside Windows

Ignore select() exceptions outside Windows. Disconnect established P2P
peers on Windows exceptions instead of probing them with recv(). Update
the Windows functional test to require disconnection.

Co-authored-by: Antoine Poinsot <mail@antoinep.com>

7dc00e68e8 http: handle socket errors separately from reads

Disconnect HTTP clients on Windows socket exceptions, including TCP
urgent data. On poll errors or hangups without read readiness,
disconnect before sending instead of attempting an unrequested read.

Co-authored-by: Matthew Zipkin <pinheadmz@pm.me>
</commits>

+def get_tcp_urgent_padding(*, linux_host):
+    """Choose padding for a message sent with send_tcp_urgent_data()."""
+    # Pad a message so that it spans several TCP segments.
+    # Only the final sentinel byte is urgent. The urgent pointer in each
+    # earlier segment then points beyond that segment's own payload, so the
+    # node sees the urgent indication, and reads that stop at the urgent
+    # mark, while the urgent byte itself is still in flight. The sentinel
+    # is not part of the message and must not be counted.
+    #
+    # On Linux the loopback maximum segment size (MSS) approaches 64 KiB,
+    # so a larger message is needed to get more than one segment.
+    # BSD-derived stacks (macOS, FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD) pass a MSG_OOB
+    # send to TCP one send-buffer chunk at a time and mark the last byte of
+    # each chunk urgent; macOS also caps chunks at 64 KiB. Keep the whole
+    # send within one chunk there. Their smaller loopback MTU still splits
+    # the message into several segments.
+    return 256 * 1024 if linux_host else 60 * 1024
+
+
+def send_tcp_urgent_data(sock, message, *, linux_host):
+    """Send a message followed by an urgent sentinel outside the message."""
+    # Fit BSD sends in one buffer chunk; keep Linux send-buffer autotuning.
+    if not linux_host:
+        sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_SNDBUF, 128 * 1024)
+    sock.sendall(message + b"U", socket.MSG_OOB)
+
+
+def pack_linger(*, enabled, timeout):
+    """Pack the socket linger settings using the Python host's native layout."""
+    # Windows struct linger contains two unsigned shorts; Unix uses two ints.
+    return struct.pack("HH" if os.name == "nt" else "ii", enabled, timeout)

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+# Copyright (c) 2026 The Bitcoin Core developers

+# file COPYING or http://www.opensource.org/licenses/mit-license.php.
+"""Test P2P handling of TCP urgent data and resets while sending."""
+
+import socket
+
+from test_framework.messages import (
+    CInv,
+    MAGIC_BYTES,
+    MSG_BLOCK,
+    MSG_WITNESS_FLAG,
+    msg_generic,
+    msg_getdata,
+    msg_ping,
+    msg_version,
+)
+from test_framework.netutil import get_tcp_urgent_padding, pack_linger, send_tcp_urgent_data
+from test_framework.p2p import NetworkThread, P2PInterface, P2P_VERSION
+from test_framework.test_framework import BitcoinTestFramework
+from test_framework.util import assert_equal, assert_greater_than, mine_large_block, p2p_port
+from test_framework.wallet import MiniWallet
+
+
+def reset_on_close(sock):
+    """Make a subsequent close send a TCP reset and discard unsent data."""
+    sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_LINGER, pack_linger(enabled=True, timeout=0))
+
+
+class SocketErrorsTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
+    def set_test_params(self):
+        self.num_nodes = 1
+        self.extra_args = [["-maxsendbuffer=1", "-maxreceivebuffer=1"]]
+
+    def run_test(self):
+        self.message_builder = P2PInterface()
+        self.message_builder.magic_bytes = MAGIC_BYTES[self.chain]
+        self.version = msg_version()
+        self.version.nVersion = P2P_VERSION
+        self.check_urgent_bytes()
+        self.check_urgent_pointer_ahead()
+        self.check_reset_while_sending()
+
+    def check_probe(self, send_probe, expected_bytes):
+        node = self.nodes[0]
+        with socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", p2p_port(0)), timeout=10) as peer:
+            self.wait_until(lambda: len(node.getpeerinfo()) == 1)
+            if self.windows_target:
+                with node.assert_debug_log(["socket exceptional condition"]):
+                    try:
+                        send_probe(peer)
+                    except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError, ConnectionAbortedError):
+                        # The node can disconnect before the bulk send finishes.
+                        pass
+                    self.wait_until(lambda: len(node.getpeerinfo()) == 0)
+            else:
+                send_probe(peer)
+                # Processing the ordinary version message demonstrates progress
+                # despite the urgent indication. The urgent byte is excluded.
+                def received_version():
+                    peers = node.getpeerinfo()
+                    assert_equal(len(peers), 1)
+                    return peers[0]["version"] == self.version.nVersion
+
+                self.wait_until(received_version)
+                assert_equal(node.getpeerinfo()[0]["bytesrecv"], expected_bytes)
+        self.wait_until(lambda: len(node.getpeerinfo()) == 0)
+
+    def check_urgent_bytes(self):
+        self.log.info("Check handling of individual urgent bytes")
+        version = self.message_builder.build_message(self.version)
+        # Use a fresh connection for each byte so earlier urgent indications
+        # cannot be overwritten before they are observed by the node.
+        for byte in b"URG":
+            def send_probe(peer):
+                peer.setsockopt(socket.IPPROTO_TCP, socket.TCP_NODELAY, 1)
+                assert_equal(peer.send(bytes([byte]), socket.MSG_OOB), 1)
+                # Windows should disconnect immediately on the urgent indication.
+                if not self.windows_target:
+                    peer.sendall(version)
+
+            self.check_probe(send_probe, len(version))
+
+    def check_urgent_pointer_ahead(self):
+        self.log.info("Check an urgent pointer ahead of ordinary P2P data")
+        padding = get_tcp_urgent_padding(linux_host=self.linux_host)
+        payload = self.version.serialize() + b"\x00" * padding
+        version = self.message_builder.build_message(msg_generic(b"version", payload))
+
+        def send_probe(peer):
+            send_tcp_urgent_data(peer, version, linux_host=self.linux_host)
+
+        self.check_probe(send_probe, len(version))
+
+    def check_reset_while_sending(self):
+        self.log.info("Check reset while the node has unsent block data")
+        node = self.nodes[0]
+        wallet = MiniWallet(node)
+        mine_large_block(self, wallet, node)
+        block_hash = node.getbestblockhash()
+        block_size = len(node.getblock(block_hash, 0)) // 2 + 24
+        peer = node.add_p2p_connection(P2PInterface(), supports_v2_p2p=False)
+        peer.sync_with_ping()
+        NetworkThread.network_event_loop.call_soon_threadsafe(peer._transport.pause_reading)

+        sent_bytes = self.wait_for_send_stall(node)

+
+
